gen-gf-pochaevsk-fs-rowan: Pochaevsk leaves every lowercase a with its mouth slightly ajar, and its bowls barely swell at the widest point. Rowan, a serif, is friendlier and more open.
gen-gf-ponomar-fs-rowan: Loud, wide-mouthed letters with a subtle thick-and-thin lilt lead in Ponomar, then hand off to the classic serif Rowan. Ponomar makes the noise and Rowan keeps the talk going.
gen-gf-potta-one-fs-rowan: Potta One looks like bent pipe cleaner, spaced out wide. Rowan, a serif, shows a slight but clear swelling in its strokes, so the heading gives way to something much more human.
gen-gf-princess-sofia-archivo: Princess Sofia writes its lowercase with a deep midsection and a hand-drawn lilt, with letters nearly touching. And Archivo, a sans, brings a commanding x-height and curves that open outward.
gen-gf-princess-sofia-fs-asap: Asap reads as open arcs, with lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals, and it feels sturdy. And Princess Sofia, hand-drawn and tightly spaced, loosens the mood above it.
gen-gf-princess-sofia-fs-epilogue: Loose, curvy, a bit cheeky: Princess Sofia pairs its deep-bellied handwriting with Epilogue, a sans-serif with stubby ascender tips and rounded-nib strokes. The handwriting and the wire-like lines make a lively mix.
gen-gf-princess-sofia-fs-erode: Hand-drawn and nearly touching, Princess Sofia sets a casual tone with deep-bellied lowercase. Erode, a serif with a tall middle band and gentle weight shifts, rewards a body size a touch larger than usual.
gen-gf-princess-sofia-fs-fira-sans: Graceful handwriting from Princess Sofia, with barely any gap between letters, sits over a body of Fira Sans. And its sans strokes carry no thick-thin contrast, so a longer passage would run smooth and steady.
gen-gf-princess-sofia-fs-public-sans: Hand-drawn, deep-bellied lowercase from Princess Sofia, with letters nearly touching, meets a hefty body in Public Sans. A plain sans sits firmly beneath the handwriting and gives it something solid to lean on.
gen-gf-princess-sofia-fs-supreme: Supreme reads as a thick, heavy strip of text through the middle, with letters held open rather than curled shut. And a longer passage would feel crisp, while Princess Sofia adds a hand-drawn note above.
